newsitem.title: JAPAN: December JGB ends Tokyo at new record high.
newsitem.headline: December JGB ends Tokyo at new record high.

text.p: The key December Japanese Government Bond (JGB) futures contract ended the Tokyo session at 125.48 on Thursday, the highest level ever for any benchmark futures contract listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
The rally was led by speculative purchases by dealers. Some cash bond buying by institutional investors was also detected.
The December ended at the day's high of 125.48, after opening at 125.12. It closed at 125.19 on Wednesday.
"Many think that a small downward correction is warranted after the recent aggressive gains that have continually renewed all-time highs," said a trader at a European bank.

However, a city bank trader said: "When everybody is waiting for a dip, the market in fact never dips, and the decisively bullish market tone is forcing people to grab bonds at a whatever price available, no matter how expensive."
In the corporate bond market, Tokyo Electric Power Co Inc (TEPCO) launched a 2.8 percent 150 billion yen bond, priced at 99.80 and due on November 29, 2006.

"The TEPCO bond was absorbed by the market in an instant. I think investors had to cover their eyes to grab the bond, because the terms are so unfavourable to buyers," a trader at a local brokerage said.
In early trade, some brokers built short positions in JGB futures to hedge against possible slow demand on TEPCO's bond.
But they had to cover positions due to good sales of the issue, accelerating the December's rise, traders said.
The bullish JGB market was little impressed by a large 17.4 percent year-on-year increase in September housing starts.
Traders said the market knew that demand for housing had peaked in September, ahead of a planned rise in the consumption tax to five percent from the current three percent from April 1.
